proposal.summary: RAM 0x3fdba4-0x3fdc39 is EEPROM 0x722-0x7b7 of the application's EEPROM mirror. cm848_applicationMain -> cm848_initEepromDriverAndLoadMirror loads EEPROM 0x0-0x1a3f at start-up, and the periodic reload (cm848_onEepromBlockRead) keeps rewriting 0x0-0x8e7. The application reads the range as four I/O configuration tables, each scanned over every entry by index: switch_input_hardware_line_cal[11..31], switch_input_datalink_source_bits_cal, logical_output_line_active_low_bits_cal and logical_output_line_cal[0..46]. The RAM dump equals the EEPROM dump byte for byte here. The boot service loop (mpc555_systemInitialization) reuses the same RAM. That loop runs only when the strap pins read high or ECM status is not CALIBRATION_VALID, and only after cm848_clearRamRegions. In it, mpc555_initHardwareConfig writes the MPC555 CMF erase / program parameters: a CMFTST enable byte, step counts, CMFCTL bases and per-step bits, 8 per-step CMFTST values for erase and for program, and per-step pulse limits. It also writes the flash2 (external flash) poll / retry limits. The naming rule I applied: a row whose address the application reads directly, or uses as a table base, keeps or takes an application name. A row the application reaches only through another base's index takes its kernel name, and its comment documents both roles. None of the QADC names had any QADC user. The program step tables become dword[8] / word[8] arrays where no application-read row sits inside (14 rows are absorbed). New word rows at 0x3fdbb4 / 0x3fdc00 / 0x3fdbd4 give the application's switch 19 line, output 18 line and the kernel's program step count their own names.

proposal.notes:
Method (scripts in /home/linux/.claude/jobs/374b0424/tmp/w15/r96/scratch/Q5/investigator/): scan_range.py walks every function window of both banks with base-register tracking (lis / addi / ori / mr / add, D-form and X-form indexed accesses). scan_range_keep.py is the same scan keeping registers across calls; it adds exactly one hit, 0x3fdc00 @0x4f138. raw_imm_scan.py checks every lis-0x40 immediate and finds no absolute hit outside the function table. dump_compare.py shows RAM == EEPROM over 0x3fdb8e-0x3fdc7c. No application store reaches the range.

Judgment calls: (1) The rule I applied: a row whose address the application reads at a fixed address, or uses as a table base, gets the application name. A row the application reaches only by index from another base gets the kernel name, because only kernel code renders it. Every comment documents both roles. (2) Two kernel table bases (0x3fdbb2 erase CMFTST, 0x3fdbfe program CMFTST) cannot be dword[8], because application-read rows sit inside them (0x3fdbb4 / 0x3fdbb6 / 0x3fdbce; 0x3fdbfe / 0x3fdc00). They stay word rows, and the kernel's dword accesses there will render with a leading underscore, and the indexed reads as casts. (3) 0x3fdbd2 shrinks from dword to word so that 0x3fdbd4 (program step count) gets a row; the application's lbzx rendering from the base does not change. (4) I added 'program' to the program-only kernel rows (cmf_program_control_base / cmf_program_pulse_control_value / cmf_program_control_step_bits / cmf_program_step_pulse_limits) to pair them with the cmf_erase_* rows. (5) Encoding: a deleted row (absorbed by an array) has proposed_name and proposed_type empty plus a 'DELETE THIS ROW' comment; there are 14 (0x3fdbe2-0x3fdbfa, 0x3fdc20-0x3fdc2c). A new row has current_name empty (0x3fdbb4, 0x3fdbd4, 0x3fdc00). 0x3fdbce is an arrays.csv row. (6) I did not name the CMFCTL bit fields (0x28000000 / 0x1e0000 / 0x4f0000 / 0xf0000) or interpret which MPC555 mask IMMR >> 16 >= 0x3030 selects; neither is proved here.
